candidates.title: Prepare a freelancer invoice draft

demandEvidence.chore: A freelancer needs to send an invoice.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: A freelancer needs to send an invoice.

experimentPlan.output: A draft invoice checklist and plain-text invoice from details supplied by a freelancer.
inputs: Fictional client name and billing address
Operator-supplied invoice date and due date
experimentPlan.trigger: A freelancer enters details for one invoice they intend to send.
steps: Collect the operator-supplied details in a fixed form.
Check that the required fields are present.
Format a plain-text invoice draft and flag blank fields.
Have the freelancer verify all amounts, terms and tax treatment.
The freelancer transfers the approved details to their chosen invoicing method and sends it.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Using fictional input with a deliberately blank due date, confirm the draft preserves supplied values and clearly flags the missing date without inventing one.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The freelancer supplies and confirms client details, amounts, terms and jurisdiction-specific tax treatment, then creates and sends the final invoice.
unverified: The post does not specify invoice fields, frequency or output format.
No invoicing software, persistence, delivery or tax calculation capability is evidenced.
Whether any freelancer would pay for this draft aid is unknown.

ease.reason: A form can organize operator-supplied invoice details, but this post gives no format or invoice-tool support.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent freelancers might pay to reduce invoice preparation; the post states a need, not willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A fictional invoice draft is small, but required fields, tax treatment and usable output format are unknown.

autonomy.reason: The proposed loop drafts text only; a person must verify amounts, tax rules and send the invoice.

evidence.reason: The literal source identifies sending an invoice but gives no frequency, fields or context for this need.

candidates.reason: Scored as a narrow proposed experiment; the provisional mean is below the frozen 6 threshold, so it is not proposed for publication.

candidates.title: Review mobile game test log CSV rows

demandEvidence.chore: A mobile game tester records battery percentage, device temperature, frame drops and notes, then transfers CSV rows to a Google Sheet; attempted triggers miss or duplicate files.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I have tried a Schedule Trigger plus Google Drive Watch Files and also a Webhook from a shortcut on the phone, but the workflow either doesn’t fire at all or fires twice on the same file.

experimentPlan.output: A review CSV that lists parsed game-test rows and flags repeated rows for a person to check.
inputs: Synthetic CSV rows with battery percentage
Synthetic CSV rows with device temperature and frame drops
An operator-selected field or combination of fields used to identify duplicates
experimentPlan.trigger: A tester supplies an exported CSV after a manual game-testing session.
steps: Read the supplied CSV into structured rows using the documented n8n extraction capability.
Apply an operator-selected key to flag or remove duplicate rows using documented n8n deduplication capability.
Preserve the original values and produce a review table with duplicate flags.
Ask the tester to inspect flagged rows and correct any parsing or identity mistakes.
The tester manually transfers approved rows to their own sheet.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fictional CSV containing one repeated row and one row with a blank measurement, verify that rows are parsed, the chosen duplicate is flagged, and the blank is not silently filled.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A tester exports and supplies the file, chooses meaningful duplicate fields, checks parsed measurements and decides what to enter in a sheet; no phone trigger or live sheet write is proposed.
unverified: The retained spans do not establish a successful phone upload trigger or file readiness check.
The references document CSV extraction and duplicate operations, not correctness on this tester’s actual CSV or Google Sheets writes.
The appropriate duplicate key and review rules must be chosen by the tester.
A paying customer and repeated commercial demand are not established.

ease.reason: n8n documents CSV extraction to JSON rows and duplicate removal, but these references do not support mobile intake or sheet writing.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small game-testing teams may pay to reduce log cleanup; this post does not establish a team buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week supplied-CSV review is bounded using documented extraction and deduplication; phone upload and Sheets flow are unresolved.

autonomy.reason: Repeated row parsing and deduplication can be automated on supplied files, but no trigger or sheet-write capability is established and a person reviews the output.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe the log fields, delayed CSV transfer and missed or duplicate triggers; frequency beyond the post is unknown.

candidates.reason: Scored as a narrow proposed experiment; the provisional mean is below the frozen 6 threshold, so it is not proposed for publication.

candidates.title: Compare ad and Shopify purchase exports

demandEvidence.chore: Export aligned 30-day Meta purchase and Shopify online order totals, then inspect unexplained differences such as possible duplicate tracking.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: In Shopify, export daily orders for the same 30 days, Online Store channel only, without test and cancelled orders.

experimentPlan.output: A table aligning supplied daily Meta purchase and Shopify order totals, with dates that differ flagged for review.
inputs: Fictional daily Meta purchase totals with the stated attribution setting
Fictional Shopify daily Online Store order totals
Operator confirmation that test and cancelled orders are excluded
experimentPlan.trigger: An ecommerce operator supplies two manually exported daily tables for the same date range.
steps: Check that both tables contain the same date range.
Compare daily totals using the operator-approved matching rule.
List missing dates and differing totals without assigning a cause.
Show the source rows beside each flagged difference.
Ask the operator to investigate tracking and approve any next action.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: With fictional tables containing a missing date and one doubled total, confirm the output flags those differences and does not label their cause as proven.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator obtains exports, confirms filters and matching assumptions, investigates tracking and authorizes changes; the proposal does not access ad or Shopify accounts.
unverified: The source is an instructional post and does not establish repeated paid demand.
No supplied reference supports account access, export automation or attribution diagnosis.
The matching rule and useful discrepancy threshold require operator review.

ease.reason: A supplied-table comparison can be mocked, but the retained spans provide no implementation reference for exports or reliable attribution analysis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: ecommerce operators might pay for export comparison; this instructional post does not establish a buyer request or payment.

feasibility.reason: A fictional table comparison fits four weeks, but matching rules and interpretation of causes remain uncertain.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable difference table is possible from supplied files, while a person must validate dates, exclusions and investigate causes.

evidence.reason: The retained spans specify aligned exports and describe attribution and possible duplicate tracking; repeated customer demand is not established.

candidates.reason: Scored as a narrow proposed experiment; the provisional mean is below the frozen 6 threshold, so it is not proposed for publication.
